definition: A data room: a folder tree of documents with its own members, groups, permission matrix, settings and activity log. Rooms move through `draft`, `live`, `closed` and `archived`.
A folder or a document in a room's tree. Permission entries, capabilities and trash all work on nodes.
One thing a person may do with a node, such as `LIST`, `VIEW`, `DOWNLOAD_ORIGINAL` or `MANAGE`. Capabilities are bits, and plugins can register their own.
The table of capabilities that groups and people hold on each folder and document, inherited down the tree. It is layer A of the two-layer check.
A named set of capabilities, such as `view`, `download` or `manager`, used when granting access instead of listing capabilities one by one.
Every operation needs both the capabilities on its node (the permission matrix) and the action from the identity system (Better IAM). Either layer can refuse.
A person's or group's role on a room in the identity system: `owner`, `admin`, `publisher`, `editor`, `contributor`, `viewer` or `auditor`. Relations decide which actions are allowed.
What the identity system decides on, in the `better-files:` namespace, such as `better-files:documents:download`.
A short-lived, signed, use-capped link that serves one file. Downloads and viewer pages are tickets, never direct storage URLs.
Each room's hash-chained record of what happened in it. `activity.verify` recomputes the chain and finds any record changed after the fact.
Someone from outside your organization invited into a room, such as a buyer or an auditor. Guests are bound by the room's guest rules and see only what the matrix grants.
A package that adds tables, capabilities, actions, endpoints, hooks or jobs to a Better Files instance, such as NDAs, watermarks or share links.
